name: Learn semaphore basics
blurb: Flag positions for each letter, based on a clock face. Almost obsolete, quick to learn, and a genuinely charming party trick at distance.
gear: Two flags, or two brightly coloured cloths
steps: Learn the eight arm positions, thought of as clock positions, and how each pair of positions maps to a letter.
Learn the alphabet in the standard circles: letters A to G use one arm low, and each subsequent circle moves the reference arm.
Learn the control signals: attention, error, numerals and end of message.
Practise spelling your name and short words in front of a mirror.
Practise sending to a partner at 50 metres, and then receiving.
Build speed until you can send a short sentence without pausing to think.
tips: Crisp, held positions read far better at distance than fast sloppy ones.
Contrast matters. Dark flags against a dark background are unreadable.
proof: You send and receive a short message with a partner at 100 metres.
